<summary>
Turn 1: Agent inspected inputs. /root/input.mp4 duration ~12.052s. target_language.txt contains “ja”. segments.srt has one window 00:00:00,000–00:00:12,116. source_text.srt has one English transcript line; reference_target_text.srt has one Japanese target line.
Turn 2: Confirmed python package edge_tts is installed.
Turn 3: Wrote /root/dub_multilingual.py pipeline: parse SRTs, generate TTS segment audio (initially via edge-tts), duration-control with atempo/pad/trim, apply filtering + fades, normalize to ITU-R BS.1770-4 loudness (ffmpeg loudnorm 2-pass, target I=-23 LUFS), render /outputs/tts_segments/seg_0.wav at 48kHz mono PCM, mix into full-length audio bed, normalize again, mux with original video to /outputs/dubbed.mp4 (AAC 48kHz mono), and write /outputs/report.json with timing/duration/drift fields.
Turn 4: Running the script failed during edge-tts synthesis with aiohttp WSServerHandshakeError 403 (invalid response status from Bing websocket), so no outputs were produced.
Turn 5: Checked for offline/local TTS tools; espeak-ng is available.
Turn 6: Tested espeak-ng Japanese voice (“-v ja”); produced WAV successfully (duration ~9.98s for a short phrase), indicating offline TTS works.
Turns 7–13: Modified dub_multilingual.py to remove edge-tts dependency and switch to espeak-ng:
- Removed edge_tts import.
- Replaced choose_edge_voice with choose_espeak_voice mapping (ja->ja etc.).
- Replaced TTS generation in make_segment_wav: runs espeak-ng to produce a WAV (via stdin), then converts/resamples to 48k mono PCM via ffmpeg, then continues duration control and loudnorm steps.
- Updated main() to call choose_espeak_voice.
Turn 14: Attempted to rerun with “rm -rf /outputs && …” but failed because /outputs cannot be removed (permission denied).
Turn 15: Attempted alternative cleanup “mkdir -p /outputs && rm -rf /outputs/* && python …” but command errored with “bash: syntax error near unexpected token `&&`”, so the script was not rerun and outputs still not generated in this trace window.
</summary>
